name: ESP32-C3

strapping.2: Chip boot mode strapping pin (with GPIO8, GPIO9). Datasheet v2.4 Table 3-3: GPIO2 does not actually determine SPI Boot vs Joint Download Boot, but it is recommended to pull it up (value 1 in both modes) due to glitches. Default at reset: floating.
strapping.8: Chip boot mode (Joint Download Boot requires GPIO8=1 with GPIO9=0; any value for SPI Boot) and UART0 ROM message printing control together with EFUSE_UART_PRINT_CONTROL. Default at reset: floating.
strapping.9: Chip boot mode select: 1 = SPI Boot (default, internal weak pull-up), 0 = Joint Download Boot (UART0 / USB-Serial-JTAG download). Holding GPIO9 low at reset enters download mode.

psram.condition: Not applicable: neither the ESP-IDF GPIO summary nor the ESP32-C3 datasheet v2.4 describes a PSRAM interface for this chip.

usb_jtag.note: GPIO18 = USB_D-, GPIO19 = USB_D+. Used by USB-Serial-JTAG by default; reconfiguring them as normal GPIOs disables USB-JTAG. If the app reconfigures these pins the device disappears from the host; recover by pulling GPIO9 low and resetting. When USB is disabled their internal weak pull-up/down are disabled by default (configurable). D-/D+ can be swapped via USB_SERIAL_JTAG_EXCHG_PINS.

notes: flash_spi: GPIO12-GPIO17 are the SPI0/1 flash pins per ESP-IDF ('usually used for SPI flash and are not recommended for other uses'; datasheet: SPIHD=GPIO12, SPIWP=GPIO13, SPICS0=GPIO14, SPICLK=GPIO15, SPID=GPIO16, SPIQ=GPIO17). GPIO11 is included because the datasheet IO MUX table maps chip pin 18 (VDD_SPI) to GPIO11 and states VDD_SPI is 'the power supply pin for flash by default, and can only be used as a GPIO pin if the flash is powered by an external power supply'. ESP-IDF's GPIO summary does NOT flag GPIO11 - treat it as an error only if the board powers flash from VDD_SPI.

Datasheet v2.4 says the chip has '22 or 16 GPIO pins' - in-package-flash variants expose fewer GPIOs (the flash pins are used internally). Do not use pins connected to in-package flash for any other purpose.

input_only / no_internal_pull are empty: datasheet v2.4 Sec. 4.1.3.1 states 'All GPIOs have selectable internal pull-up or pull-down' and 'All digital IO pins are bi-directional'; TRM v1.4 Register 5.21 IO_MUX_GPIOn_REG (n: 0-21) has FUN_WPU/FUN_WPD for every GPIO.

jtag order is [MTMS, MTDI, MTCK, MTDO] = [GPIO4, GPIO5, GPIO6, GPIO7] (ESP-IDF configure-other-jtag page and datasheet IO MUX table). By default JTAG is routed to the built-in USB_SERIAL_JTAG; burning DIS_USB_JTAG eFuse moves it to GPIO4-GPIO7.

ADC2: ESP-IDF stable (v6.1) ADC oneshot page: 'ADC2 oneshot mode is no longer supported, due to hardware limitations. The results are not stable. This issue can be found in ESP32-C3 Series SoC Errata. For compatibility, you can enable CONFIG_ADC_ONESHOT_FORCE_USE_ADC2_ON_C3 to force use ADC2.' The ADC continuous page likewise says ADC2 DMA is no longer supported (CONFIG_ADC_CONTINUOUS_FORCE_USE_ADC2_ON_C3_S3). Datasheet: 'ADC2 of some chip revisions is not operable' and ADC2 is not factory-calibrated. Errata ADC-183 ('The Digital Controller (DMA) of SAR ADC2 Cannot Work') affects revisions v0.0-v1.1, workaround 'use SAR ADC1', no fix scheduled. Recommend flagging any ADC2 (GPIO5) use.

adc2_wifi_conflict is null: the current ESP-IDF stable C3 ADC oneshot/continuous pages contain no ADC2-vs-Wi-Fi restriction text; the documented restriction is the ADC2 hardware limitation above. Older IDF releases may have had different wording - not checked.

ADC hardware limitation (all ADC): RNG uses ADC as an entropy source, so random numbers are less random while adc_oneshot_read() runs; a given ADC unit can only be in oneshot OR continuous mode at a time.
Strapping timing: hold time tH min 3 ms after CHIP_EN high before strapping pins become regular IO.
RTC/deep-sleep wake: only GPIO0-GPIO5 can wake the chip from Deep-sleep; others only from Light-sleep. GPIO0/GPIO1 are also XTAL_32K_P/N.
Radio: datasheet title '2.4 GHz Wi-Fi (802.11b/g/n) and Bluetooth 5 (LE)' - no Bluetooth Classic.
Data sourced from ESP-IDF stable = v6.1 docs, ESP32-C3 datasheet v2.4, ESP32-C3 TRM v1.4, retrieved 2026-10-28.

conditional.11: VDD_SPI flash power pin — only usable as GPIO when the flash is powered externally (eFuse VDD_SPI_AS_GPIO); datasheet
